The implementation of requiredLength (lines 13-17, `Objects.requireNonNull(text, "text")`) still enforces its documented precondition, so after the diff the pair is asymmetric at the implementation level while symmetric at the contract level. Any architectural reasoning that treats 'nullable* vs required*' as a naming-based precondition contract (the only stated design signal in the module) is now violated for the nullable side, meaning the module's naming/Javadoc conventions no longer predict behavior for one of its two public APIs.

assumptions: The naming convention and paired Javadoc are the module's intended architectural contract, as no other design artifacts exist in the snapshot.
requiredLength's refactor to a local variable is behavior-preserving (verified against diff hunk).
reasoningSummary.conclusion: The module's naming/Javadoc convention no longer reliably predicts enforced behavior for nullableLength, while the sibling it is documented against still honors its contract. This is an architectural consistency defect at the module's public boundary, fixable by aligning implementation and documentation on both sides.
counterexamples: If the two methods were never intended as a symmetric pair and nullableLength's name is merely historical, the asymmetry is cosmetic rather than a contract defect — but the unchanged Javadoc line 8 argues against treating it as purely cosmetic.
No caller in the snapshot couples the two methods, so no runtime path currently exercises the asymmetry; the finding is about contract predictability, not an observed failure.

reasoningSummary.rule: In a single-type utility module whose only design signal is method naming plus paired Javadoc, sibling methods advertised as complementary preconditions should enforce those preconditions; a change that makes one side violate its naming/Javadoc while the other keeps enforcing it removes the naming as a reliable contract indicator.

originalFinding.suggestion: Make the pair internally consistent: restore nullableLength's null-tolerant body to match its name and Javadoc, or explicitly re-document both methods so the naming convention and preconditions are aligned and no longer misleading for API consumers.
